definitions.explanation: A sale in which buyers compete by offering increasingly higher prices. Especially associated with early-morning fish and produce auctions at Japanese wholesale markets like Tsukiji and Toyosu. From the verb 競る (to compete, to bid).

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}の{競|せ}りが{始|はじ}まった。
{豊洲|とよす}{市場|しじょう}の{競|せ}りを{見学|けんがく}した。
examples.english: I observed the auction at Toyosu Market.

examples.japanese: {初|はつ}{競|せ}りで{一番|いちばん}マグロが{三億円|さんおくえん}で{落札|らくさつ}された。
examples.english: The top tuna was sold for 300 million yen at the year's first auction.

notes:
CULTURE:
Japan's wholesale fish market auctions are famous worldwide. The {初|はつ}{競|せ}り (first auction of the year) at Toyosu Market regularly makes international news when record prices are paid for premium tuna, a tradition symbolizing good fortune for the new year.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {初|はつ}{競|せ}り (first auction of the year)
- {競|せ}りにかける (to put up for auction)
- {競|せ}り{落|お}とす (to win at auction)
- {競|せ}り{値|ね} (auction price)
- {魚|さかな}{市場|しじょう}の{競|せ}り (fish market auction)
